clue.text: Tweet to thwart censure at last

parts.note: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly, thwarting them

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word censure

parts.note: the final letter of censure

explanation.surface: Someone takes to social media to dodge a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' looks like a social media post, but here it is the sound a bird makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to make a high chirping sound, as a small bird does.

clue.text: Quick and brilliant black winger through on the outside

indicators.note: a word sitting on the outside wraps around the pieces that come before it

parts.note: per means through or by way of
ace means excellent
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a winged creature, a bird

explanation.surface: Praise for a fast, dazzling footballer of colour playing out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'quick' is a fast bowler; the surface pretends winger means a footballer, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang calls any fast bowler a quick, the noun standing for the whole phrase.

clue.text: Mine working for Spike useful in upward mobility?

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A mine in operation produces a spike that helps people get on in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upward mobility' sounds like social climbing; the question mark signals it means actual climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal peg hammered into rock to secure ropes for climbers.

clue.text: Opening somehow meant for severe critic

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of meant arrive in some unspecified new order

parts.note: a hatch is an opening in a deck or wall
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An opening line somehow intended for a harsh reviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a person hired to make savage attacks on others' reputations, a ruthless detractor.

clue.text: Cunning fellows housed in suitable accommodation

indicators.note: things housed in something sit inside it, so these pieces go within the outer word

parts.note: apt means fitting or suitable
art can mean craftiness or cunning
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Crafty men are lodged in suitable rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms used as a home, which is a kind of living space.

clue.text: Observe that judge has left target for tabloid?

indicators.note: if a word has left, its letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: to observe a festival is to celebrate it
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Someone notices a judge walking out, the sort of story the tabloids love.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove RATE from CELEBRATE to leave CELEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous people, short for celebrities, are the favourite subjects of gossip newspapers.

clue.text: Cover of loveless work penned by revolutionary author

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, as in a pen
something revolutionary turns round, so the writer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a novel is a literary work; loveless means without love, the tennis zero O, so that letter goes

explanation.surface: A dust jacket for an unromantic book by a radical writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, hence the letter O; 'Cover' looks like a noun for a book jacket but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or surround completely, so it is a verb for cover.

clue.text: Traveller to drive back, lukewarm about P&O

indicators.note: back says the word for drive is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force in

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so lukewarm goes around the letter P

parts.note: something cool is not quite warm
taken as written
taken as written, added after the ampersand

explanation.surface: A trip on a ferry company's boat leaves a passenger unenthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a British ferry and cruise line; here it is simply P and O, with only the P going inside COOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant famous for his journey to China, the archetypal explorer and voyager.

clue.text: Vegetable energy going into upped swan?

indicators.note: in a down entry, upped means turned to read upwards, so backwards
going into places the energy symbol inside the other word

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A veg-powered swan taking flight, absurdly.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scottish and northern English word for a turnip or swede.

clue.text: Positive result for Formula One team's head

parts.note: pro means in favour of
F for Formula and I, the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of team

explanation.surface: A team boss in motor racing hoping for a good result.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial gain, money made beyond costs, is a favourable outcome of a business.

clue.text: Screech animal near a rock face heard

indicators.note: heard says to go by how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: a cat next to a wall, which is a sheer face of rock

explanation.surface: A shriek rings out from a creature beside a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent CAT A WALL sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to make a shrill howling cry like a cat at night.

clue.text: Monkey shown without tail in animation

indicators.note: without tail says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the vervet is an African monkey

explanation.surface: A cartoon features a tailless monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animation' suggests cartoons, but it means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve is energy and enthusiasm, the same spirited liveliness meant by animation.

clue.text: Assist insect swallowing close to sunken well

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the insect word encloses a letter

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: the close to a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of sunken
fit means well or healthy

explanation.surface: An insect drinking near the bottom of a well needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' sounds like a shaft for water, but it is the adjective for healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To benefit something is to help it or do it good, a verb for aid.

clue.text: Everything written into autonomous program for election

indicators.note: something written into a program is put inside it

parts.note: a bot is a program that runs on its own
all means everything

explanation.surface: A bot is coded with everything it needs to run a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a secret vote, the process by which people choose candidates.

clue.text: Soy trade disrupted after doctor cooked without oil

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor causes upheaval in the soya trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts and similar snacks dry-roasted are heated in an oven with no fat added.

clue.text: Rapid series of visits organised to Welsh pits and to old city

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the following letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters rearranged
taken as written
Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A trip is arranged to the coal mines of Wales and to an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop tour is a quick journey with brief stops at many places, as campaigning politicians make.

clue.text: Roman historian discounting first class colleges

indicators.note: discounting first means leaving out the opening letter

parts.note: Livy wrote a history of Rome
a league is a class or level, as in out of my league

explanation.surface: A classical scholar ignoring a top-grade set of universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' reads as one phrase; split it so first goes with discounting and class stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is a group of eight old, prestigious universities in the north-eastern United States.

clue.text: Bar limits changes leading to group loyalty

indicators.note: changes says the preceding letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: New restrictions on a pub make the regulars close ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong allegiance to one's own clan or faction, often hostile to outsiders.

clue.text: Mayor in Barnet has almost beaten Labour

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of has is dropped
beaten as in battered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
has without its final letter

explanation.surface: A local mayor in a London borough has nearly defeated the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a borough of north London, and Labour looks like the political party; it is one of the twelve labours of Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: Capturing the wild beast of Mount Erymanthus alive was the fourth task set for Hercules.

clue.text: An adolescent male dressed at last in rubber finding wealth

parts.note: an is the article a
a lad is a boy or youth

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of dressed

parts.note: the final letter of dressed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teenage boy kitted out in latex strikes it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' suggests the material, but it means one who rubs: the hero rubbed a lamp and found a genie.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale the youth polishes a magic lamp, releasing a genie who brings him riches.

clue.text: Worm that is wrapped around in anorak

indicators.note: something wrapped in another is covered by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, a nerd

indicators.note: turned around, the abbreviation for that is runs the other way

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A worm is found wrapped up in a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is a hooded jacket, and in Britain also a nerdy obsessive, the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nereids are a family of marine bristle worms such as the ragworm, named after sea nymphs.

clue.text: Smear live fish ingesting uranium

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: ingesting means taking inside, so the fish word holds the element symbol

parts.note: the dab is a small flatfish
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A slur against living fish contaminated with radioactive metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or plaster something with a sticky substance like paint.

clue.text: He was a Dutch painter? Utter nonsense

indicators.note: to utter is to speak aloud, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: bosh is informal for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the claim that a man was a Dutch painter as complete rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was the Netherlandish artist of nightmarish fantastical scenes such as The Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: Roman general an old man seizing control

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the outer words clutch the control word

parts.note: an is the article a
an old man is a father, pa
a grip on something is control of it

explanation.surface: A military commander staging a coup, as old men in power do.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's leading commander, victor at the naval battle of Actium.

clue.text: Fitness expert rare commodity in Middle East?

parts.note: PE is physical education
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A personal trainer is scarce in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a wry definition by example rather than a dictionary one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting calm without war has been in short supply in that troubled region for decades.

clue.text: Getting rook inside sack is a game

indicators.note: inside places the chess piece within the other word

parts.note: a bag is a sack
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: Stuffing a bird into a sack is treated as sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook looks like the crow, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Brag is a British card game similar to poker, played for stakes with three-card hands.

clue.text: American soldier coming in to deliver for firm

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the soldier goes inside the other word

parts.note: to deliver from is to rid or free
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier arrives to make a delivery for a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' suggests a courier, but means set free; 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and unbending, the adjective sense of firm.

clue.text: Dependable but left out, is worker acknowledged?

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: solid means reliable
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A reliable employee left out of things wonders whether he is recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a loose definition: the answer means self-styled, someone acknowledged only by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: French for so-called: a title one claims or that is merely asserted, not genuinely held.

clue.text: Eco-friendly member shows talent in garden

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly
a member is a limb or digit

explanation.surface: An environmentalist party member is a gifted gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests someone in a club; here it is a body part. The phrase is American, where Britons say green fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for natural skill at making plants grow and thrive.

clue.text: Pearl: article buried in garden plot?

indicators.note: something buried in soil lies inside it, so the article goes within

parts.note: a flower bed is a plot in a garden
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A precious pearl found buried in a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a small round gem threaded on a string, a kind of bead.
